title: Separate timestamp anchoring for burst-credit backfills to prevent invoice ghost-lines
creator: Avery Patel
description: Background: We continue to see intermittent 'ghost' invoice lines (small negative/zero-value lines) surface after late usage backfills and burst-credit corrections. Root cause analysis points to two interacting issues: (1) the backfill pipeline uses event timestamps from the origin system without aligning to the export anchoring policy, and (2) the export reconciler merges overlapping hour buckets using a naive earliest-timestamp anchor which can split proration across invoice boundaries when late events arrive. Problem: these ghost-lines cause customer confusion and require manual investigation; they also break downstream Netsuite import checks which reject idempotency of line fingerprints. Goal: redesign timestamp anchoring for all burst-credit and late-usage backfill flows so that exported invoice line generation is deterministic, idempotent, and stable across retries and replay. Success criteria: exported billing manifests show zero ghost-lines in a 24h shadow run against last 30 days of historic late-usage data; downstream Stripe/Netsuite exports apply without rejected lines for the same replay; automated reconciler end-to-end tests pass and maintain idempotence (re-running job produces identical export). Constraints: must be backwards-compatible with existing invoice-line schema and not change customer-facing invoice numeric totals except to correct previously incorrect proration splits. We must maintain performance of hourly export window (target: <30s extra CPU per tenant on export job). Proposed approach: 1) introduce a canonical anchor calculation for backfills: anchor = max(hour_bucket_start, floor_to_minute(event_received_at, 15m_granularity)) for burst-credit adjustments, and floor_to_minute(event_effective_at, 1m_granularity) for usage pulses; 2) add a per-tenant per-day seqnum (export_seq) attached to each line to enforce deterministic merge ordering; 3) expand export manifest to include fingerprint_v2 (sha256 over tenant, export_seq, anchor, amount) to avoid Netsuite rejections from timestamp jitter; 4) add a 15-minute grace merge window to the reconciler when combining lines inside the same invoice period to absorb late microsecond-level jitter; 5) implement an offline simulation harness (billing_export_simulator_v2) that replays historical late-usage and burst-credit streams and validates idempotency and fingerprint stability; 6) create a shadow-run mode for three days before rollout, monitor metrics, and then migrate traffic. Acceptance criteria: PR merged with unit + integration tests; three-day shadow-run produces no more than 0.01% change in invoice line count vs baseline and zero rejected Lines on Netsuite staging import. Rollout plan documented in Confluence.
